governance.note: This run is miso9 (pjm-seam-hranchor) PLUS one new structural lever: a measured per-year nuclear refueling/maintenance availability overlay for MISO. MISO was the ONLY multi-year ISO with no nuclear availability overlay (the CAMPD/CEMS outage source is fossil-only — CEMS has no nuclear), so MISO nuclear ran flat at the static-pattern x (1 - EFORD) ceiling, ~97.9 TWh / ~97% CF EVERY year, vs measured 87.2/90.4/90.7 — a systematic +10.7/+7.5/+7.2 TWh over-injection. The lever populates NUCLEAR_MONTHLY_CF_BY_YEAR['MISO'] (and the static NUCLEAR_MONTHLY_CF['MISO'] forecast fallback) via scripts/derive_nuclear_monthly_cf.py --isos MISO: monthly CF = fleet EIA-923 net generation / (fleet pmax x hours-in-month), capped at 1.0. This is a MEASURED unit-availability input (rule #12: 'unit outage windows (a physical availability event)') — the staggered ~18-24 month refueling cadence, an exogenous physical-availability event identical in form to the CAMPD fossil outage overlay already in the model, and EXACTLY the same mechanism already accepted for ERCOT/CAISO/PJM/NYISO/NEISO. Forward analogue: refueling outages are scheduled 1-2 years ahead and the static seasonal pattern is the forecast-year fallback; the availability responds to changed conditions (retirements/additions/dormant units via NUCLEAR_DORMANT_UNTIL). It is applied as an availability UPPER BOUND, not a generation floor; the LP still dispatches nuclear economically within it (nuclear's near-zero MC means it runs to the bound, so realized energy lands at measured 87.2/90.2/90.6 — by faithful availability, not by an output pin: no monthly net-gen is forced as an equality, no value is rescaled so the model output lands on actuals, the deration is blind to the price/volume residual). Reproduces measured annual nuclear energy within <1 TWh/yr with the real refueling seasonality. derive_nuclear_monthly_cf.py --check passes; 18 nuclear tests pass. All other levers unchanged from miso9: per-year measured PJM-seam marginal-heat-rate anchor, priced import/export node via reference-price interface, Manitoba firm-hydro import block, per-plant CAMPD tranche binning, historic CAMPD unit-outage windows, measured F923 per-plant monthly delivered fuel, EIA-923 biomass must-run. No adder/haircut/sigmoid tuned to a residual; no unit pinned to its observed CEMS generation; no input rescaled to land output on actuals.
governance.open_misses_note: Honest open structural misses (documented, NOT masked — the nuclear lever is kept on rule-#1 faithfulness grounds even where it worsens a residual): (1) The nuclear derate removes ~7-11 TWh/yr of phantom must-run nuclear, and in 2023/2024 the LP backfills the freed load with MORE imports rather than domestic thermal (2024 net import 48.3 -> 52.3 TWh; 2023 63.6 -> 69.3 vs actual 23.1/37.9) — because at the margin the priced seam is cheaper than the next domestic coal/gas unit. This does NOT mean the derate is wrong (rule #1): it UNMASKS the over-import as the dominant remaining injection error rather than causing it. The fix is the seam, not reverting nuclear: the un-anchored SPP (flat HR 10.0) and South/SOCO (flat 12.0) seams + import-node level over-serve are the next lever (task Part 4 SPP anchor). (2) 2025 net-interchange sign-flips the other way (model +3.4 TWh net export vs actual -19.0 net import; import-hours 45.8% vs 79.2%) driven by the persistent 2025 coal over-run (model 236.8 vs actual 192-201) making MISO long — a coal-offer/merit-order root cause the nuclear lever does not touch. (3) CT_PEAKER remains a real ~16 TWh merit-order under-generation (model ~3 vs measured ~19); the classifier is correct/consistent (see the miso9 attestation CORRECTION) and CT recovers only once the over-import is fixed and peakers clear. (4) Domestic gen runs ~43 TWh under EIA-930 net gen in 2024 (the over-import mirror); coal -18/-18/+45 and gas vs EIA-923 track the same seam + 2025-coal root causes. These are the next levers, not residual fits.
